mastodon:
Shipped a small thing: Mise, a mobile client for Mealie — the self-hosted recipe manager I run at home.

Android APK + iOS from source, GPL-3.0, no account, no analytics, no server of mine. It only talks to your instance.

Built around the twenty minutes you spend cooking, not the ten you spend browsing.

https://github.com/TheValkDokk/mise-mealie

alt: Cream card reading “Mise — Dinner, decided.” with two phone screens: tonight's pasta plan and a dark cook-mode step.

mastodon: Cook mode is the reason it exists: one step at a time, 26pt type, black screen, and the entire surface is a tap target — so you can advance it with the back of a knuckle when your hands are covered in flour.

alt: A single recipe instruction in large cream type on a near-black screen, with “STEP 1 OF 4” above it and a thin ember progress bar.

mastodon: The rest is quiet: tonight's dinner as a full-bleed card, a photography-first cookbook, and a shopping list where one button pulls every recipe on the next seven days of the plan into the list.

mastodon:
The field isn't empty — Ghee, Mealie Go, Meshi Plan all exist, and Ghee is free. Two reasons to build a fourth: GPL-3.0 means it can't quietly become a paid app later, and cooking is the centre of the design instead of a feature on a checklist.

Gaps, plainly: read-only, no offline queue, one list.
